questions.title: Upload + link + embed handled in one place vs. separate features
Organisation model (flat list / folders / sections tied to course structure)

references.title: Course editor file upload area
references.question: Q1
references.take: Teachable places course material upload directly in the lesson editing context, keeping the add-material action close to the course structure.

references.title: Attach existing file or link chooser
references.question: Q1
references.take: A chooser for existing content makes attachment a selection task alongside upload, a useful pattern for mixed file and external-resource inputs.

references.title: Add material from course editor
references.question: Q1
references.take: Teachable shows an in-editor add-material affordance, supporting a single place to introduce course assets.

references.title: Course content organized in sections
references.question: Q2
references.take: The course view groups learning content into visible sections, making the section hierarchy the primary organization model.

references.title: Course curriculum with ordered lessons
references.question: Q2
references.take: Teachable presents materials as an ordered curriculum, tying resources to course sections rather than a standalone flat file list.

references.title: Lesson resources in course structure
references.question: Q2
references.take: Skillshare keeps lesson resources inside the class progression, reinforcing course-tied sections as the learner-facing organization.

references.title: Mobile lesson with video and resources
references.question: Q1
references.take: Udemy combines the lesson video with a nearby resources affordance, showing how media and downloadable material can coexist in one lesson surface.

references.title: Mobile course lesson media surface
references.question: Q2
references.take: Coursera’s lesson surface keeps the learner in a course sequence while presenting lesson media, supporting structure-led consumption.

references.title: Adding a file flow
references.question: Q1
references.take: Podia’s three-step file flow separates choosing, uploading, and completion states while keeping the task focused on adding one course asset.

references.title: Adding a PDF flow
references.question: Q1
references.take: Teachable’s PDF flow exposes a dedicated document path with multiple confirmation stages, indicating file type can shape the add-material journey.

references.title: Adding a course module flow
references.question: Q2
references.take: Kajabi’s module creation flow makes the section/module container an explicit step before adding content, tying organization to course authoring.
